page: The Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with Hyper-Threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 12.0 GB of system memory, which provides 3.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 260 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain any GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of average and weak performance metrics, reflecting its shared CPU allocation. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and Passmark CPU scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core performance is limited, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core result and a poor rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance also shows a split profile: cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 421.33 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.96 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which introduces potential resource contention and explains the weaker multi-core and database benchmark results, such as the weak Passmark database operations score. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high storage-to-compute ratio with 260 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside 12.0 GB of RAM, making it a viable option for workloads that require fast local storage but do not demand sustained, intensive multi-core CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, basic Redis caching, single-threaded file compression tasks, and lightweight development environments.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core CPU performance and cached memory bandwidth, contrasted by weak multi-core scaling and uncached memory throughput.
